title: throughput-benchmarking-harness-and-methodology-wip-6
summary: Working doc describing the throughput benchmarking harness design, load-generator configs, repeatability practices, warmup strategy, and measurement methodology for the serving runtime. Focused on producing stable, comparable throughput numbers across model variants, hardware, and config changes.
content:
Purpose:
This document captures our current approach for throughput benchmarking of the serving runtime. Goal is to produce repeatable, defendable numbers for tokens/sec and request/sec under realistic request shapes while controlling for caching, batching, and warmup artifacts.

Scope:
- Online text generation endpoints (autoregressive decoders)
- Configurable sequence lengths and prompt shapes
- Batching and KV-cache behavior
- GPU- and CPU-bound serving nodes
- Both single-model and model-fallback policy scenarios

Key design principles:
1) Repeatability over absolute peak: build harness that yields consistent numbers across repeated runs and different engineers.
2) Isolate variables: change one knob at a time (batching, sequence length, quantization) and keep everything else fixed.
3) Measure steady-state: avoid transient warmup artifacts contaminating measurements.
4) Collect rich telemetry: per-request latencies, GPU utilization, host CPU, memory, power (if available), queue lengths, batching stats, and model cache hit rates.

Harness components:
- Controller: orchestrates experiments, starts/stops load generators, collects metrics, and writes run metadata.
- Load-generator (lg): lightweight process that emits requests according to a workload profile. Supports shaping by tokens-per-request, prompt templates, sampling seeds, concurrency and RPS modes.
- Metrics collector: pulls Prometheus metrics, NVML/GPU stats, and application traces.
- Artifact sink: stores run logs, raw request traces, and aggregated summaries (CSV + JSON metadata).

Workload profiles:
- Microbench: single short prompt, short output length (e.g., 16 in / 16 out) to stress small-seq throughput.
- Standard gen: mix of prompt lengths (8/32/64) with output lengths proportional to input, representing product traffic.
- Long-context: e.g., 1024 input + 256 output to measure KV-cache and memory effects.
- Mixed-concurrency: Poisson arrival process at target RPS to emulate real traffic bursts.

Load generator config (examples):
- Mode: concurrency (N outstanding requests) or rps (target requests/sec)
- Ramp: linear ramp-up duration (default 60s)
- Steady window: measurement window after ramp (default 240s)
- Warmup iterations: number of warmup requests per worker (default 100)
- Seed: random seed for prompt selection (must be recorded)

Example lg command (shell snippet):
./lg \
  --profile standard-gen \
  --mode rps --target-rps 200 \
  --workers 16 \
  --ramp 60 \
  --steady 240 \
  --warmup 100 \
  --seed 42 \
  --prometheus-endpoint http://collector:9091/push \
  --payload-templates templates/standard.json

Warmup strategy:
- Two-tier warmup: (1) micro warmup to prime kernels and JIT paths, (2) full warmup to fill KV caches and reach steady batching patterns.
- Micro warmup: run short bursts of 50-200 requests with minimal inter-request interval. Good for ensuring kernels and allocators are initialized.
- Full warmup: run until per-second throughput and p95 latency stabilize (heuristic: 3 consecutive 30s windows with <5% variance) or until configurable warmup request count is reached.
- For experiments measuring cold-start effects, warmup must be disabled and cold-start behavior documented separately.

Measurement windows and metrics:
- Ignore initial ramp and warmup. Measurement starts at t = ramp + warmup, and continues for the steady window.
- Primary metrics: tokens/sec (total tokens emitted / steady_window), requests/sec, p50/p90/p95/p99 latency (end-to-end), server-side compute latency, queueing time, batch size distribution, GPU utilization, GPU memory headroom, cache hit rate.
- Secondary metrics: system CPU, ephemerals (e.g., disk IO), network RTT, NVLink utilization.
- Export raw per-request traces (request id, start_ts, end_ts, prompt_len, output_len, batch_id) to artifact sink for offline analysis.

Aggregation and reporting:
- For each run produce a single-line summary CSV with: run_id, date, commit_hash, model, hardware, batch_config, concurrency/rps, seed, ramp_secs, warmup_policy, steady_secs, tot_tokens, tokens_per_sec, avg_batch_size, p50,p90,p95,p99 latencies, error_rate, gpu_util, notes.
- Store full JSON metadata alongside artifacts. Metadata keys must include commit_hash and lg_config.
- When comparing runs, use identical metadata except the variable under test.

Repeatability practices:
- Version everything: controller, load-generator, model artifact (hash), serving container image digest, and benchmark scripts. Record these in run metadata.
- Fixed random seeds for prompt selection and sampling. Record seed in metadata.
- Deterministic templates: keep prompt templates pinned to exact strings and template versions.
- Environment capture: record kernel versions, CUDA/CUDNN/driver versions, and visible devices.
- No other noisy workloads on the node. Use dedicated test infra or cgroups to isolate.
- Run each experiment N times (recommended 5) and report median with IQR. Flag runs where variance > 10% for tokens/sec.

Controlling for caching and batching artifacts:
- KV-cache priming: when measuring long-seq performance, ensure the cache is primed to reflect steady-state KV behavior unless measuring cold cache.
- Batch formation: batch size distribution depends on concurrency and request shape. Control desired average batch by tuning number of workers, max_batch_size, and scheduling window. Capture per-batch histograms.
- Cache warmup policy: for multi-tenant benchmarks, create a background traffic generator that simulates cross-tenant cache pollution to measure robustness.

Common failure modes and mitigations:
- Spiky results due to transient GC or memory pressure: monitor host memory and JVM/Python GC metrics. Increase swap/oom buffers or run multiple repetitions.
- Overloaded GPU queues causing high p99 latency: reduce target RPS or increase concurrency to favor batching.
- Inconsistent load-gen clock skew across workers: ensure ntp/chrony sync before runs.
- Missing artifact capture: fail the run if metrics collector RPC fails.

Analysis heuristics and derived metrics:
- Effective tokens/sec = total_generated_tokens / steady_window_seconds. Report both client-observed and server-confirmed tokens/sec and reconcile differences.
- Batch efficiency = sum(batch_size * compute_time) / (total_compute_time). Use to estimate wasted compute due to underfilled batches.
- Latency breakdown: client->LB, LB->server-queue, queue->compute-start, compute-duration, compute-end->client. Identify dominant components.

Example experiment matrix (recommended baseline runs):
- Baseline: model A on GPU type X, batch_size cap 8, concurrency mode N=32, sequence 32/64, quantization FP16.
- Variants: change one dimension per run: (a) max_batch_size=16, (b) quantization=4-bit, (c) sequence length 128, (d) extra worker processes per node.
- Run each variant 5 times, report median and IQR.

Artifacts and storage:
- Store raw lg logs, per-request CSV, Prometheus scrape files, GPU telemetry (NVML logs), and aggregated summary CSV. Compress artifacts and upload to artifact store with run_id.

Checklist before a benchmark run:
- [ ] Controller at released tag (record tag)
- [ ] Serving image digest recorded
- [ ] Model artifact hash recorded
- [ ] Nodes isolated (no other tenants)
- [ ] NTP synced
- [ ] Prometheus target reachable and recording
- [ ] lg seed recorded and payload templates checked

Open questions / TODOs:
- Standardize a minimal JSON schema for run metadata (run_id, commit, image_digest, model_hash, hardware, lg_version, seed, args). (ACTION: @Ethan)
- Add automated detection for steady-state (variance threshold) instead of fixed steady window. (ACTION: @Marisol)
- Investigate automated margin-of-error reporting for tokens/sec across repeats. (ACTION: @Jin)

Notes and references:
- See existing docs in this folder: throughput-benchmarking-harness-and-methodology.json and wip variants for historical runs and prior heuristics.
- GitHub PR with harness changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/throughput-harness/pull/42
- Jira ticket for dashboarding: JIRA-RT-314

Recommended next steps for this draft:
- Stabilize the minimum run schema and add CI gating that rejects benchmark PRs that do not include run metadata.
- Implement seed capture and deterministic prompt selection in lg.
- Add an optional background cache-polluter mode to the harness to test multi-tenant effects.

End of doc.
